title: Moussaka
subtitle: Greek beef and aubergine bake with bechamel topping
excerpt: Layers of roasted aubergine, spiced beef ragu and rich bechamel, baked until golden. The defining dish of Greek home cooking, and well worth the effort.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from classic Greek moussaka preparations across multiple culinary sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze fully assembled and baked. Cool completely, portion and freeze. Reheat from frozen in a 180 C oven for 45 minutes, covered in foil for the first 30.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The meat sauce can be made 2 days ahead. The whole assembled dish keeps refrigerated for up to 2 days unbaked; add 10 minutes to the baking time.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 160 C. The bechamel needs moderate heat to set without splitting.

content.text: Moussaka has three components: roasted aubergine, a cinnamon-scented beef ragu and a thick bechamel. None is difficult, but each needs to be done properly before assembly. The aubergine must be roasted until completely soft and a little caramelised; undercooked aubergine is bitter and spongy. The ragu should be rich and dry, not wet. The bechamel must be thick enough to set into a firm layer when baked. Rest the finished dish for at least 20 minutes before serving or it will collapse when cut.

items.prepNote: divided: for roasting aubergine and frying the meat sauce

content.text: Salt and roast the aubergine. Preheat the oven to 200 C (fan 180 C). Lay the aubergine slices on two baking trays, brush both sides with olive oil and season with salt. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once halfway, until the slices are completely soft and golden at the edges. Remove and set aside. Reduce the oven temperature to 180 C (fan 160 C) for the final bake.

Make the meat sauce. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan over high heat. Add the beef mince in a single layer and cook without stirring for 3 to 4 minutes until browned underneath. Break up and stir, then cook for another 3 minutes until all moisture has evaporated and the meat is caramelised. Add the onion, reduce the heat to medium and cook for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Add the tomato puree and stir for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, bay leaves and oregano. Season well. Simmer over medium-low heat for 25 to 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and nearly dry: it should not be saucy. Discard the bay leaves.

Make the bechamel. Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and whisk for 2 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste. Gradually pour in the warm milk, whisking constantly, until smooth. Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce is very thick: it should coat the back of a spoon heavily. Remove from the heat, add the nutmeg and season. Allow to cool for 5 minutes, then whisk in the beaten egg yolks quickly (do not add them while the sauce is boiling hot or they will scramble).

Assemble the moussaka. Use a roasting tin roughly 30 cm x 20 cm x 6 cm deep. Arrange half the aubergine slices in a single layer on the base. Spread all the meat sauce evenly over the top. Arrange the remaining aubergine slices over the meat sauce. Pour the bechamel over the top and spread evenly. Scatter the grated parmesan over the bechamel.

Bake at 180 C (fan 160 C) for 45 minutes until the top is deeply golden and the edges are bubbling. Remove from the oven and rest for at least 20 minutes before cutting into portions. This resting time is not optional: the layers need to set or they will slide apart.

items.cause: The milk was added too quickly or the sauce was not whisked constantly.
items.fix: Push the sauce through a sieve and return to the pan. Whisk vigorously over low heat. Next time, add the milk in a slow, steady stream while whisking.

items.symptom: Portions collapse when cut and served
items.cause: The moussaka was not rested long enough after baking.
items.fix: Always rest for at least 20 minutes. The layers need this time to firm up. If serving a crowd, rest for up to 40 minutes: it stays hot inside.

items.symptom: Meat sauce is too wet and makes the layers soggy
items.cause: The ragu was not reduced enough before assembly.
items.fix: The meat sauce must be almost dry: if you scrape a spoon through it, no liquid should pool in the gap. Simmer for longer with the lid off to evaporate moisture.

items.cause: The aubergine was not cooked long enough, or old aubergine was used.
items.fix: Roast until completely soft and collapsing at the edges. Salting the aubergine slices for 30 minutes before roasting (then rinsing and patting dry) also draws out bitterness, though this step is not always necessary with fresh aubergine.
